place.castelgrande.name: Castelgrande
place.castelgrande.desc: It occupies a rocky promontory over two hundred metres long; the oldest surviving part dates from the 10th century. Two great towers rise above the complex, the Torre Bianca (White Tower) and the Torre Nera (Black Tower). Also known as Castel Vecchio, San Michele Castle or Uri Castle, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000, together with Montebello, Sasso Corbaro and the walls.
place.castelgrande.visit.text: Open all year: until 18 March 2027 daily 10:30-16:00 (last admission 15:30), in summer 10:00-18:00; adults CHF 15, reduced CHF 8.
place.castelgrande.timeline.0.title: From prehistory to the Romans
place.castelgrande.timeline.0.text: The hill has been inhabited for over 7000 years, as shown by Neolithic settlements of the 6th millennium BC, Roman outposts and the first fortifications, from the 4th century AD.
place.castelgrande.timeline.1.title: Lombards and Franks
place.castelgrande.timeline.1.text: Lombards and Franks are recorded here between the 6th and 8th centuries; from the early 11th century the castle belonged to the bishop of Como, who had a residence there.
place.castelgrande.timeline.2.title: The present castle
place.castelgrande.timeline.2.text: The complex seen today dates from a first building phase in the 13th century, overlaid by a second, “Milanese” phase between 1473 and 1486.
place.castelgrande.timeline.3.title: Uri Castle, then San Michele Castle
place.castelgrande.timeline.3.text: After Bellinzona came under Confederate sovereignty (1500) it was named Uri Castle, in 1506; after the Canton of Ticino became independent (1803) it was called San Michele Castle, from 1818.
place.castelgrande.timeline.4.title: Museum and UNESCO heritage
place.castelgrande.timeline.4.text: It houses the museum of history and archaeology; together with the other two castles and the walls it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
place.montebello.name: Montebello Castle
place.montebello.desc: Probably built in the 13th century by the Rusca family of Como and mentioned indirectly in 1313, it was enlarged with new walls between 1462 and 1490. It was also called Schwyz Castle and later San Martino Castle. Today it houses the archaeology and history section of the civic museum; it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
place.montebello.visit.text: Castle and museum closed until 18 March 2027 (the courtyards can still be visited); in season daily 10:00-18:00, adults CHF 10.
place.montebello.timeline.0.title: The Rusca
place.montebello.timeline.0.text: The castle was built at the end of the 13th century as a residence by the Rusca, a Ghibelline family from Como.
place.montebello.timeline.1.title: The Visconti
place.montebello.timeline.1.text: When the Visconti took power in Como, the castle passed to the lords of Milan. The stronghold was protected by a high circuit wall with swallowtail (Ghibelline) merlons and corner towers, a moat and a wooden drawbridge.
place.montebello.timeline.2.title: Enlargement
place.montebello.timeline.2.text: The castle was enlarged and strengthened, with a second, more massive circuit wall and towers with a rounded plan.
place.montebello.timeline.3.title: Schwyz Castle, then San Martino Castle
place.montebello.timeline.3.text: Under Confederate rule it took the name Schwyz Castle, in 1506; after 1818 it was called San Martino Castle.
place.montebello.timeline.4.title: Museum and UNESCO heritage
place.montebello.timeline.4.text: It houses an archaeological museum; together with the other two castles and the walls it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
place.sasso-corbaro.name: Sasso Corbaro Castle
place.sasso-corbaro.desc: The last of Bellinzona's castles to be built: the Duke of Milan had it built from 1479, after the defeat at Giornico in 1478, to prevent the barrier formed by the two castles below and the walls from being outflanked from the hillside above. It is also known as Cima Castle, Unterwalden Castle or Santa Barbara Castle. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000 and hosts temporary exhibitions.
place.sasso-corbaro.visit.text: Castle and exhibitions closed until 18 March 2027 (the courtyards can still be visited); in season daily 10:00-18:00, adults CHF 15.
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.0.title: A watchtower
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.0.text: From the end of the 14th century a tower for controlling and watching over the surrounding area is documented on the hill.
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.1.title: The Sforza fortress
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.1.text: In the first months of 1479 work began on the present castle, a typical Sforza fortress. The architect Benedetto Ferrini died of plague in the autumn; the work was completed by the ducal engineer Gabriele Ghiringhelli.
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.2.title: Also a prison
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.2.text: Besides its defensive role, the castle served as a place of detention: an escape is documented in 1494.
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.3.title: Unterwalden Castle, then Santa Barbara Castle
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.3.text: From 1506 it was called Unterwalden Castle, and from 1818 Santa Barbara Castle.
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.4.title: Exhibitions and UNESCO heritage
place.sasso-corbaro.timeline.4.text: It is the only fortification in Bellinzona not connected to the others; its rooms host exhibitions. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
place.murata.name: Murata
place.murata.desc: Wall running west from Castelgrande that served to bar the valley floor between the castle and the River Ticino: a double crenellated curtain wall with a vaulted passage inside. It was rebuilt in 1486-1487 under the direction of Gabriele Ghiringhelli; in 1515 a flood of the Ticino destroyed about 150 metres of it, which were never rebuilt. It is part of the UNESCO site of the castles of Bellinzona.
place.murata.visit.text: Access from the outer courtyard of Castelgrande, from Via Carlo Salvioni 12A or from Viale Portone (between nos. 39 and 41); opening hours and price are not published.
place.murata.timeline.0.title: The first wall
place.murata.timeline.0.text: The Visconti of Milan closed off the valley floor between Castelgrande and the Ticino with a wall: the Fortress of Bellinzona website dates it to after the Visconti conquest of 1340, other sources to after the Battle of Arbedo in 1422.
place.murata.timeline.1.title: The wall doubled
place.murata.timeline.1.text: In the Sforza period, because of the Confederates' growing ambitions, the Murata was reinforced and enlarged with a second wall.
place.murata.timeline.2.title: The bridge over the Ticino
place.murata.timeline.2.text: On the orders of Duke Ludovico Sforza a bridge, also known as the Ponte della Torretta, was built to close the valley from Castelgrande to the right bank of the river (sources give 1487 or 1489).
place.murata.timeline.3.title: The Buzza di Biasca
place.murata.timeline.3.text: In May 1515 the flood of the Ticino known as the “Buzza di Biasca” destroyed the bridge and about 150 metres of the Murata.
place.murata.timeline.4.title: UNESCO heritage
place.murata.timeline.4.text: It has been part of the UNESCO site of the castles of Bellinzona since 2000; it is reached from the outer courtyard of Castelgrande, from Via Carlo Salvioni 12A or from Viale Portone.
place.collegiata.name: Collegiate Church of Santi Pietro e Stefano
place.collegiata.desc: Renaissance church with Baroque elements and seat of the town parish, built from 1515 to 1543 on the foundations of the earlier church of Santo Stefano. The bell tower was built between 1567 and 1573, and the façade was faced with Castione stone between 1640 and 1654. It holds the large holy-water stoup known as the Fontana Trivulzio, dating from 1465.
place.collegiata.visit.text: Visiting hours not published on the pages consulted; the church is in Piazza Collegiata.
place.collegiata.timeline.0.title: Santo Stefano
place.collegiata.timeline.0.text: The church of Santo Stefano stood on the site; it is recorded from 1424 and was consecrated in 1473.
place.collegiata.timeline.1.title: The new church
place.collegiata.timeline.1.text: The present building, in Renaissance style, was built on the foundations of Santo Stefano.
place.collegiata.timeline.2.title: Bell tower and façade
place.collegiata.timeline.2.text: Work on the bell tower began in 1567; between 1640 and 1654 the façade was faced with Castione stone.
place.collegiata.timeline.3.title: The choir
place.collegiata.timeline.3.text: The choir was enlarged from 1684; work on this part of the church continued until 1785.
place.collegiata.timeline.4.title: The parish church
place.collegiata.timeline.4.text: It is the church of the town parish, restored three times in the 20th century (the interior between 1990 and 1999). It holds the holy-water stoup known as the Fontana Trivulzio, dating from 1465.
place.piazza-del-sole.name: Piazza del Sole
place.piazza-del-sole.desc: Town square whose design, dated 1996-1999, is listed among the works of the Ticino architect Livio Vacchini.
place.piazza-collegiata.name: Piazza Collegiata
place.piazza-collegiata.desc: Pedestrian square in the centre, overlooked by the Collegiate Church of Santi Pietro e Stefano (Piazza Collegiata 20).
place.piazza-nosetto.name: Piazza Nosetto
place.piazza-nosetto.desc: Pedestrian square in the centre, where Bellinzona's town hall stands.
place.palazzo-civico.name: Town Hall (Palazzo Civico)
place.palazzo-civico.desc: Town hall built in 1924 in Renaissance style, replacing a 15th-century municipal building. It has a clock tower and an inner courtyard with two tiers of loggias.
place.palazzo-civico.timeline.0.title: The municipal building
place.palazzo-civico.timeline.0.text: A 15th-century municipal building stood on the site.
place.palazzo-civico.timeline.1.title: The new building
place.palazzo-civico.timeline.1.text: The present town hall was built in Renaissance style, with a clock tower and an inner courtyard with two tiers of loggias.
place.palazzo-civico.timeline.2.title: The town hall
place.palazzo-civico.timeline.2.text: It is the city's town hall, in Piazza Nosetto.
officials.dicastero.Educazione, cultura,: Education, culture, youth and social affairs
place.palazzo-orsoline.name: Palazzo delle Orsoline
place.palazzo-orsoline.desc: Built in 1738 as an Ursuline convent, it passed to the canton under the 1848 law suppressing the convents. Today it houses the Grand Council and the Council of State of the Canton of Ticino; the first session of the Grand Council was held in its refectory on 26 August 1803.
place.teatro-sociale.name: Teatro Sociale
place.teatro-sociale.desc: The city's main theatre, in Piazza Governo, built between 1846 and 1847 to designs by the Milanese architect Giacomo Moraglia and opened on 26 December 1847. It is an Italian-style theatre, with wooden boxes on three levels. In the 1990s it underwent a conservative restoration, completed in 1997.
place.teatro-sociale.visit.text: The theatre box office opens only on performance days (45 minutes before evening shows, 30 before afternoon ones); advance sales at the InfoPoint, Piazza Collegiata 12, and on Ticketcorner; guided tours on request at the InfoPoint.
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.0.title: Construction
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.0.text: It was built by the engineer Von Mentlen to a design by the Milanese Giacomo Moraglia and opened on 26 December 1847; it could hold 700 spectators.
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.1.title: First alterations
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.1.text: Maurizio Conti added a section for the club rooms (casinò sociale), now a restaurant (in 1894 according to some sources, in the 20th century according to others); in 1919 the building was adapted to new uses and the load-bearing beams were renovated.
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.2.title: Cinema, then abandonment
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.2.text: In 1950 it was converted into a cinema; after closing in 1970 it stood abandoned until the work of the 1990s.
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.3.title: The restoration
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.3.text: Between 1990 and 1997 (from 1992 according to other sources) the architects Giancarlo Durisch, Pia Durisch and Aldo Nolli restored the foyer, auditorium and façades with conservative interventions; the stage machinery was rebuilt.
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.4.title: Italian-style theatre
place.teatro-sociale.timeline.4.text: It is the city's main theatre, with 300 seats: for Switzerland, a rare example of a 19th-century opera house still in use.
place.stazione.name: Bellinzona railway station
place.stazione.desc: The city's main railway station, in service since 1874, when the first Ticino sections of the Gotthard railway opened; the complete line, through the Gotthard tunnel, opened in 1882. For long-distance trains it is the first station south of the Gotthard Base Tunnel. Completely renovated, it was officially reopened on 15 October 2016.
place.villa-dei-cedri.name: Villa dei Cedri
place.villa-dei-cedri.desc: Late neoclassical 19th-century villa in Ravecchia, set in a park whose large cedars give it its name. Bought by the municipality in 1978, since 1985 it has housed the city's art museum, devoted to art from Ticino, Lombardy and Switzerland from the 19th century to the present day.
place.villa-dei-cedri.visit.text: Museum: Wed–Thu 14:00-18:00, Fri–Sun and public holidays 10:00-18:00, closed Monday and Tuesday; adults CHF 12, reduced CHF 8, free up to 16 years of age. Park open daily 07:00-18:00 in winter (07:00-20:00 from April to September).
place.santa-maria-delle-grazie.name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
place.santa-maria-delle-grazie.desc: Franciscan church built together with the friary of the Friars Minor between about 1480 and 1495, and consecrated in 1505. It retains its original Gothic form, with a simple gabled façade; inside, a large rood screen is frescoed with scenes of the Life and Passion of Christ. It was devastated by fire on 31 December 1996; the frescoes were later restored.
place.santa-maria-delle-grazie.visit.tex: Visiting hours not published on the pages consulted; the church is at Via Convento 5.
The church was built, together with the friary of the Friars Minor, between about 1480 and 1495.

The rood screen was frescoed with a large Crucifixion and fifteen scenes from the life of Christ. The date is disputed: between 1495 and 1505 according to some critics, around 1513–1515 according to the most recent.
It was consecrated in 1505 and dedicated to Santa Maria delle Grazie.
On 31 December 1996 a fire devastated the building; the rood screen frescoes were later restored.
It retains its original Gothic form, with the simple gabled façade and the frescoed rood screen.
place.san-biagio.name: San Biagio
place.san-biagio.desc: Parish church of Ravecchia, first mentioned in 1237. The gabled façade of exposed stone is decorated with 14th-century frescoes, including a gigantic St Christopher; the interior has a nave and two aisles. The restorations of 1912-1914 returned it to its medieval appearance.
place.ponte-torretta.name: Ponte della Torretta
place.ponte-torretta.desc: Two arches remain of the ten-arch stone bridge completed in 1815: the others were demolished in 1969 to build the A2 motorway. They are joined by the arched pedestrian and cycle bridge in Corten steel, 172 metres long and built in 2021-2022, which spans the River Ticino and the motorway.
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.0.title: Ludovico il Moro's bridge
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.0.text: At the end of the Murata, Ludovico il Moro had a bridge built over the Ticino (sources give 1487 or 1489).
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.1.title: The Buzza di Biasca
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.1.text: In May 1515 the flood of the Ticino known as the “Buzza di Biasca”, caused by the collapse of the natural dam that a landslide on Monte Crenone had formed in 1513, destroyed the bridge and about 150 metres of the Murata.
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.2.title: The stone bridge
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.2.text: The ten-arch stone bridge was completed, linking the town directly to Locarno again after three centuries. The tower known as the Torretta, which gives the bridge its name, was demolished around 1820.
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.3.title: The motorway
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.3.text: The bridge was demolished to build the A2 motorway, except for two arches on the east side.
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.4.title: The footbridge
place.ponte-torretta.timeline.4.text: The two arches are joined by the arched pedestrian and cycle bridge in Corten steel, 172 metres long, built in 2021–2022 over the Ticino and the motorway.
place.stadio-comunale.name: Stadio Comunale
place.stadio-comunale.desc: Multi-purpose sports ground used mainly for football, including the home matches of the Bellinzona club, and for athletics. It was officially opened on 25 May 1947; the first match had been played there on 1 December 1946.
place.stadio-comunale.visit.text: Tickets for AC Bellinzona matches on advance sale on Ticketcorner; the stadium ticket offices open 90 minutes before kick-off.
place.san-rocco.name: San Rocco
place.san-rocco.desc: The church originated in the will of Jacopo Cattaneo, who in 1330 asked for it to be built under the name of Santa Maria del Ponte. Almost completely razed, it was rebuilt in 1478; the façade was redone in 1832.
place.san-giovanni.name: Church of Santi Giovanni Battista ed Evangelista
place.san-giovanni.desc: Built from 1760 onwards to a design by Gaetano Matteo Pisoni for the Augustinian friars, it was still unfinished in 1812, and in 1834 it was turned into an arsenal. It was completed only at the end of the 20th century.
place.chiesa-rossa.name: Chiesa Rossa (San Paolo)
place.chiesa-rossa.desc: Church in Arbedo called “Rossa” (red) for the colour of its façade. It is first mentioned in 1255, but excavations have uncovered foundations from the 7th-8th century; the Romanesque bell tower dates from the 12th-13th centuries. In the 15th century it was largely rebuilt and enlarged.
place.chiesa-rossa.visit.text: No fixed opening hours: the key can be collected from the parish of Arbedo, Via alla Chiesa 18 (tel. 091 829 11 39).
place.palazzo-franscini.name: Palazzo Franscini
place.palazzo-franscini.desc: The canton's cultural centre, opened in 1999, the result of a competition won in 1988 by the architect Luca Ortelli. Among other institutions it houses the Bellinzona Cantonal Library, the State Archives of the Canton of Ticino and the Centre for Dialectology and Ethnography.
place.tribunale-penale-federale.name: Federal Criminal Court
place.tribunale-penale-federale.desc: Court of the Swiss Confederation with its seat in Bellinzona, where it began its work in 2004. Through its Criminal Chamber it tries the cases that the law places under federal criminal jurisdiction.
place.san-bernardo.name: San Bernardo
place.san-bernardo.desc: Church above Monte Carasso built at the end of the 11th century and enlarged in the 15th; the bell tower and portico date from the 16th century. The interior is almost entirely covered with frescoes, the oldest of which date from the 15th century; those on the façade date from 1582.
place.san-bernardo.visit.text: Open for visits with a guide from April to October, Thursday to Sunday 11:00-16:00 (July and August 10:30-16:30); from November to March no hours published, groups on request on 058 203 14 50.
place.ponte-tibetano.name: Carasc Tibetan Bridge
place.ponte-tibetano.desc: Pedestrian suspension bridge (a “Tibetan” bridge) between the territories of Monte Carasso and Sementina. It was officially opened in 2015.
place.ponte-tibetano.visit.text: Reached on foot, or by the Monte Carasso-Mornera cable car, getting off at Curzútt; no opening hours, seasonal closures or admission ticket are published.
place.sacro-cuore.name: Church of the Sacro Cuore
place.sacro-cuore.desc: Convent church built between 1934 and 1936 to a design by the brothers Carlo and Rino Tami; it has been a national historic monument since 1986. The interior walls bear a large Way of the Cross (Via Crucis) frescoed by Guido Gonzato.
place.fortino-ai-scarsitt.name: Fortino Ai Scarsitt
place.fortino-ai-scarsitt.desc: One of the five Camorino towers of the defensive line designed by General Guillaume-Henri Dufour and built south of Bellinzona in 1853–1854, along the Morobbia and the Sementina valley. The works employed about 500 men for a couple of years, giving work to many people reduced to poverty: this is why people called them the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortino-ai-scarsitt.visit.text: Waymarked trail of about 2 hours from Camorino Piazza, open in all seasons; guided tours on request from the Associazione Fortini della Fame.
place.fortino-ai-munt.name: Fortino Ai Munt
place.fortino-ai-munt.desc: One of the five Camorino towers of the defensive line designed by General Guillaume-Henri Dufour and built south of Bellinzona in 1853–1854, along the Morobbia and the Sementina valley. The works employed about 500 men for a couple of years, giving work to many people reduced to poverty: this is why people called them the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortino-ai-munt.visit.text: Waymarked trail of about 2 hours from Camorino Piazza, open in all seasons; guided tours on request from the Associazione Fortini della Fame.
place.fortino-ala-pelera.name: Fortino Ala Peléra
place.fortino-ala-pelera.desc: One of the five Camorino towers of the defensive line designed by General Guillaume-Henri Dufour and built south of Bellinzona in 1853–1854, along the Morobbia and the Sementina valley. The works employed about 500 men for a couple of years, giving work to many people reduced to poverty: this is why people called them the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortino-ala-pelera.visit.text: Waymarked trail of about 2 hours from Camorino Piazza, open in all seasons; guided tours on request from the Associazione Fortini della Fame.
place.fortino-al-sass-del-camosc.name: Fortino Al Sass del Camósc
place.fortino-al-sass-del-camosc.desc: One of the five Camorino towers of the defensive line designed by General Guillaume-Henri Dufour and built south of Bellinzona in 1853–1854, along the Morobbia and the Sementina valley. The works employed about 500 men for a couple of years, giving work to many people reduced to poverty: this is why people called them the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortino-al-sass-del-camosc.visit.t: Waymarked trail of about 2 hours from Camorino Piazza, open in all seasons; guided tours on request from the Associazione Fortini della Fame.
place.fortino-al-pian-di-bur.name: Fortino Al Pian di Bur
place.fortino-al-pian-di-bur.desc: One of the five Camorino towers of the defensive line designed by General Guillaume-Henri Dufour and built south of Bellinzona in 1853–1854, along the Morobbia and the Sementina valley. The works employed about 500 men for a couple of years, giving work to many people reduced to poverty: this is why people called them the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortino-al-pian-di-bur.visit.text: Waymarked trail of about 2 hours from Camorino Piazza, open in all seasons; guided tours on request from the Associazione Fortini della Fame.
place.fortini-torre-murata.name: Wall tower (Torre della murata)
place.fortini-torre-murata.desc: Sementina and Monte Carasso section of the defensive line designed by General Dufour and built in 1853–1854: it made use of the valley of the Sementina stream, with massive walls, never completed, marking off the valley's entrance on the right bank of the Ticino. Like the Camorino towers on the other side of the valley, it is one of the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortini-mura-portale.name: Walls and gateway of the Fortini
place.fortini-mura-portale.desc: Sementina and Monte Carasso section of the defensive line designed by General Dufour and built in 1853–1854: it made use of the valley of the Sementina stream, with massive walls, never completed, marking off the valley's entrance on the right bank of the Ticino. Like the Camorino towers on the other side of the valley, it is one of the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.fortini-torre-monte-carasso.name: Fortini tower (Monte Carasso)
place.fortini-torre-monte-carasso.desc: Sementina and Monte Carasso section of the defensive line designed by General Dufour and built in 1853–1854: it made use of the valley of the Sementina stream, with massive walls, never completed, marking off the valley's entrance on the right bank of the Ticino. Like the Camorino towers on the other side of the valley, it is one of the “fortini della fame” (hunger forts).
place.ex-ospedale-ravecchia.name: Former Ravecchia hospital
place.ex-ospedale-ravecchia.desc: Building at Via Federico Pedotti 14, in Ravecchia, which housed the old hospital. It belongs to the Swiss Confederation and has housed the Military Police. In 2019 Bellinzona's city executive (Municipio) agreed a price of 4.6 million francs with armasuisse to buy it and turn it into a centre for culture and local associations; in 2020 the city withdrew from the purchase because the Confederation needed the premises.
place.chiesa-daro.name: Church of Santi Pietro martire, Quirico e Giulitta
place.chiesa-daro.desc: Parish church of Daro. Already mentioned in 1173, it was completely rebuilt in the 15th century; the parish house was added in 1775. It has a single nave with cross vaulting and side chapels.
place.chiesa-artore.name: Church of San Sebastiano
place.chiesa-artore.desc: Church in Artore, formerly known as “Madonna della Salute”. Only the apse remains of the medieval Romanesque building; it was altered several times until its complete renovation in 1858, when the semicircular choir was added.
place.chiesa-carasso.name: Church of Sant'Andrea
place.chiesa-carasso.desc: Late Baroque church in Carasso. Built in Romanesque style before 1285, it was destroyed and rebuilt at the beginning of the 16th century and altered again in the 18th (the portal bears the year 1735). It was restored in 1983, with altar, ambo and baptismal font by Ivo Soldini, and again in 2004; it has a Kuhn organ inaugurated in 1984.
place.chiesa-camorino.name: Church of San Martino
place.chiesa-camorino.desc: Parish church of Camorino, Romanesque in origin and already documented in 1237. In the 17th and 18th centuries it was enriched with Baroque decoration; the new apse was built in 1888. The red façade has a Renaissance portal of 1533. The 1994 restoration brought the stained-glass windows and furnishings by Nag Arnoldi.
place.chiesa-arbedo.name: Church of Santa Maria Assunta (Arbedo)
place.chiesa-arbedo.desc: Church in Arbedo, the parish church until 1583. Built in the Middle Ages, it was rebuilt in the 16th century and enlarged in 1625; the two side chapels and the baptismal font were added in the 17th century. It retains remains of Gothic frescoes, and paintings by Baldassarre Orelli in the choir.
place.chiesa-san-giuseppe-arbedo.name: Church of San Giuseppe (Arbedo)
place.chiesa-san-giuseppe-arbedo.desc: Church in Arbedo built in 1969 to a design by the architect Giampiero Mina.
place.chiesa-giubiasco.name: Church of Santa Maria Assunta (Giubiasco)
place.chiesa-giubiasco.desc: The main Catholic church of Giubiasco. Built in the 12th century, probably on the site of an older church (Santa Maria di Plumasca or Primasca, mentioned in a deed of 929), it was enlarged in the 15th century and then in Baroque style in the 17th. It was restored several times in the 20th century, most recently in 1997.
place.chiesa-san-giobbe.name: Church of San Giobbe
place.chiesa-san-giobbe.desc: Church in Giubiasco, by Piazzetta Mario Chiattone.
place.chiesa-san-bartolomeo.name: Church of San Bartolomeo
place.chiesa-san-bartolomeo.desc: Church at San Burtulumee, in the territory of Camorino.
place.chiesa-santa-maria-neve.name: Church of Santa Maria della Neve
place.chiesa-santa-maria-neve.desc: Church on the hillside above Ravecchia, along the Sentiero Prada.
place.chiesa-trinita.name: Church of the Santissima Trinità
place.chiesa-trinita.desc: Church at Pedmúnt, in Monte Carasso.
place.chiesa-evangelica.name: Evangelical Reformed Church
place.chiesa-evangelica.desc: Church of the Evangelical Reformed community, at Viale Stefano Franscini 1.
place.chiesa-sementina.name: Church of San Michele
place.chiesa-sementina.desc: Parish church of Sementina. Construction began in the 14th or 15th century to replace the church of Sant'Eusebio at Moia, destroyed by a flood; in 1440 it became the parish church. It was enlarged in 1625 and again in 1761, when it took on its present late Baroque appearance.
place.chiesa-monte-carasso.name: Church of Santi Bernardino e Girolamo
place.chiesa-monte-carasso.desc: Church at Orenno, in Monte Carasso, built between the 11th and 12th centuries. It was a wing of the convent of the Augustinian nuns, founded around 1450 and suppressed in 1859. The choir was added between 1658 and 1660; the past century has seen several restorations, including the one by Luigi Snozzi (1987-1993).
place.chiesa-pianezzo.name: Church of Santi Giacomo e Filippo
place.chiesa-pianezzo.desc: Parish church of Pianezzo, in the Valle Morobbia. The church is mentioned as early as 1371; the present building was erected in the 16th century, incorporating walls of the earlier late Gothic church. Two paintings of 1557 survive on the façade, showing St Christopher and the patron saints.

place.oratorio-santa-marta.desc: Oratory in the old town, next to the Collegiate Church of Santi Pietro e Stefano.

place.info-point.desc: Tourist office of Bellinzona e Valli Turismo, at Piazza Collegiata 12: information, tickets and advance sales for the Teatro Sociale. Tel. +41 91 825 21 31.
place.info-point.visit.text: InfoPoint Bellinzona, Piazza Collegiata 12: in winter Mon–Fri 09:00-18:00, Saturday 09:00-16:00, Sunday and public holidays 10:00-16:00; tel. +41 91 825 21 31.
place.motto-della-croce.name: Motto della Croce
place.motto-della-croce.desc: Summit at 1254 m above sea level on the slopes east of the city.
place.funivia-mornera.name: Monte Carasso–Mornera cable car
place.funivia-mornera.desc: Cable car that climbs from the village of Monte Carasso (230 m above sea level), via the restored hamlet of Curzútt (600 m), to the Alpe Mornera at 1347 m. From there you can continue on foot to the Alpe Albagno, at 1867 m.
place.funivia-mornera.visit.text: Runs daily 06:30-21:30 (no service on Wednesdays 08:00-10:00); adult return CHF 11 to Curzútt and CHF 21 to Mornera.
place.curzutt.name: Curzútt
place.curzutt.desc: Restored hamlet on the hillside above Monte Carasso, at about 600 m above sea level; intermediate stop of the cable car that climbs from the village to the Alpe Mornera.
place.convento-agostiniane.name: Old Augustinian convent
place.convento-agostiniane.desc: Former convent of the Augustinian nuns, founded around 1450 and suppressed in 1859. From 1987 to 1993 the architect Luigi Snozzi, who redesigned the centre of Monte Carasso from the 1980s onwards, converted it into a primary school and cultural centre.
place.parco-giochi-gerretta.name: Gerretta playground
place.parco-giochi-gerretta.desc: Playground in Via Vallone, reopened in March 2026 after renovation: wooden playhouses linked by balancing and climbing routes, three slides and swings.
place.parco-giochi-guisan.name: Via Henri Guisan playground
place.parco-giochi-guisan.desc: Unfenced playground in the city centre, with a tower and slide, rope climbing structures, swings and public toilets.
place.parco-giochi-bolla.name: Bolla playground
place.parco-giochi-bolla.desc: Playground in the Semine district, next to the cemetery, renovated by the city in 2026: climbing and balancing areas, slides, swings and a table-tennis table.
place.parco-giochi-montebello.name: Montebello playground
place.parco-giochi-montebello.desc: Playground by Montebello Castle, marked on the map of the official Fortress of Bellinzona website.
place.bagno-pubblico.name: Municipal swimming pool (Bagno pubblico)
place.bagno-pubblico.desc: Open-air pools at Via Mirasole 20, open from May to September: Olympic-size pool, non-swimmers' pool, diving pool and children's pool.
place.parco-giochi-pianezzo.name: Pianezzo playground
place.parco-giochi-pianezzo.desc: Play area in Pianezzo's municipal park, in the Valle Morobbia, along Via alle Scuole.

place.percorso-vita.name: Percorso Vita fitness trail
place.percorso-vita.desc: Outdoor fitness trail on the Ticino floodplain: a 2.6 km loop with 10 m of climb and exercise stations along the way. It starts at the Ponte della Torretta, where the marker shows the start. Free and open to all; it is trail no. 330 of the Zurich vitaparcours network, run by the City of Bellinzona.
place.parco-calistenico.name: Calisthenics park
place.parco-calistenico.desc: Outdoor gym in the stadium area, between the Ex Stallone car park and the artificial pitch, opened in 2026: bars at different heights, parallel bars and other calisthenics stations. Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; the equipment may be used from the age of 14, or by anyone taller than 140 cm. Its position on the map is approximate.
